findings.title: Materials' 58-point lens gap signals earnings hope
findings.body: Materials sits at the 88th percentile on trailing earnings but only the 29th on forward estimates, a 58-point gap that is the widest in the table. The market is underwriting 120 percent earnings growth next year, which at this extreme looks like a bet on a cyclical snapback rather than a reflection of current profitability.

findings.title: Energy priced for earnings rebound despite selloff
findings.body: Energy's forward P/E percentile fell 15 points in a month to 39, yet its trailing percentile remains high at 84, leaving a 46-point gap between the two lenses. The 68 percent implied earnings growth suggests analysts expect a sharp profit recovery, so the multiple compression may already be pricing in a cyclical trough.

findings.title: Health Care's forward multiple at record high
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E percentile hit 100 after a 22-point monthly jump, even as its trailing percentile sits at 85. The 47 percent compression between forward and trailing multiples means investors are paying an unprecedented premium for projected earnings, an extreme that hinges entirely on those forecasts materializing.
